To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CEGIS is a powerful framework for formal synthesis; (2) CEGIS can be applied to any program that is a recursive function; (3) The power of CEGS depends on the type of counterexamples generated and the amount of memory available; (4) The speed of convergence depends on the size of the candidate program space.

(1) CEGIS can learn any program that computes an r.e. language, (2) the convergence rate of CEGIS depends on the teaching dimension of the language, (3) the convergence rate is independent of the memory available to the synthesizer, and (4) CEGIS is more powerful than CEGIS where the counterexamples are restricted to a finite set.

(a) CEGIS can be viewed as a special case of OGIS; (b) CEGIS is a sound and complete algorithm for learning any program computing a recursive language; (c) CEGIS with bounded memory converges in a finite number of rounds if and only if the universe of candidate program is finite; (d) The speed of convergence of CEGIS is related to the notion of the teaching dimension.
